stem:
A 68-year-old man with pulmonary fibrosis has lungs that resist expansion, and his work of breathing is increased.

Compared with a healthy lung, which of the following best describes the effect of his reduced lung compliance on pulmonary ventilation?

options.label: A
options.text: A larger potential lung volume for any given distending force
options.misconception: The direction of the compliance-volume relationship is being reversed.
options.explanation: Greater compliance permits greater stretch and volume; reduced compliance, as in fibrosis, limits both.

options.label: B
options.text: An increase in the resting pressure gradient driving airflow
options.misconception: A stiffer lung is being assigned a larger driving gradient.
options.explanation: A low-compliance lung requires more effort to generate the same volume change; the resting gradient is not increased as a compensatory feature.

options.label: C
options.text: An increase in alveolar surface tension from excess surfactant
options.misconception: Surfactant's effect on surface tension is being inverted.
options.explanation: Surfactant reduces surface tension; fibrosis stiffens the lung through tissue change, not through surfactant excess.

options.label: D
options.text: A decrease in airway resistance during quiet breathing
options.misconception: A flow-resistance change is being substituted for an elasticity change.
options.explanation: Airway resistance is set by airway diameter and surfaces; parenchymal stiffness (compliance) is a separate property that is reduced in fibrosis.

options.label: E
options.text: A smaller potential lung volume for any given distending force
options.misconception: None; reduced compliance means less stretch and therefore less achievable volume.
options.explanation: Lung compliance is the ability of the lungs to stretch; the more the lungs can stretch, the greater the potential volume, so a stiff, low-compliance lung achieves a smaller volume.

context: Learning objective: apply lung compliance. Compliance is the ability of the lungs to stretch; greater stretch permits greater potential volume, so reduced compliance (fibrosis) limits volume.
